items.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: And I know Joshua had already played at the Village Vanguard and played with his father and probably Ed Blackwell and a number of different people.

ctx.x: It made it so that people who had never heard of me before had now heard of me. So I guess that did something for me. I think I got one gig directly related to that. So in terms of work, not really. And I don’t think it got me any record deals or anything like that. There were no record companies climbing around me. They’re all climbing around number one. Number two and the rest were out pretty much, we’re on our own. But we

all, not me so much, but many of the other guys already had been working with people. They were already pretty high profile professional guys. I think the prerequisite, or one of the prerequisites to be in the competition was that you did not have a leader recording released on a major label. But there was no prerequisite, you know, you can’t have worked with a jazz legend. Because these guys certainly had. I mean I know, among others, I know Chris Potter was working with Red Rodney at that time. And some of the…
How the heck do you make a living after you graduate from college and you’re out pursuing a career in jazz? How did you manage that?
